observation.content: Five synthetic publications repeat or strengthen one target claim while their declared trace leads to a single synthetic primary observation.
observation.provenance: Declared synthetic fixture; no real publication or factual claim is represented

problem_domain: Claim-relative source independence, semantic drift, and evidence aggregation in a synthetic publication chain

competence.rationale: Competence is declared only for structural evaluation of the supplied synthetic trace; no automatic source verification or semantic classification is claimed.

calibration.internal_confidence_rationale: Confidence in any substantive claim is intentionally unquantified because this fixture evaluates only the declared process structure.
calibration.external_evidence_rationale: Document count is not converted into evidence strength; the five derivative texts share one declared evidence root for the exact target claim.

evidence_sources.description: In a small exploratory sample, X under condition Z was associated with Y; causality was not tested.
evidence_sources.provenance: Synthetic primary observation declared by the fixture
evidence_sources.quality_note: Limited exploratory scope; no causal inference or generalization beyond the declared sample is supplied.

reference_frame.scope: Independence must be evaluated for one atomic target claim and a named dimension; publication count, semantic fidelity, causal status, and evidential support are not interchangeable frames.
assumptions: For the exact target claim Q1, all five synthetic derivative texts ultimately trace to synthetic-primary-observation-q1.
The derivative chain progressively changes possibility, causal status, scope, or communicative function.
Other claims within the same hypothetical documents may have different provenance and are outside this evaluation.
Repeated or stronger wording does not by itself add an independent observation.

constraints.description: Do not treat the number of derivative texts as the number or strength of independent evidence roots for the target claim.

hypotheses.statement: The texts substantially preserve the target claim but repeat one evidence root.
At least one derivative changes modality, causal status, scope, or communicative function.
Additional independent evidence roots exist but are not established by the supplied trace.
The documents may be dependent for Q1 while remaining independent for other claims or evidence dimensions.

candidate_actions.description: Define the atomic target claim, trace each derivative to its evidence root, and preserve semantic differences before aggregating support.

effects.expected_benefit: Publication count remains separate from independent evidence count for the target claim.
effects.expected_cost: Claim extraction and provenance tracing require additional review.

effects.expected_benefit: Later summaries can retain scope, modality, causal status, and unresolved dependence.
effects.expected_cost: A single consensus score remains unavailable until provenance is resolved.

candidate_actions.rationale: Claim-level tracing can be revised when additional primary evidence or corrected derivation paths become available.
candidate_actions.rollback_cost: Recompute the claim graph and any downstream aggregation from the corrected trace.

items.description: The current contract does not encode whether the five wordings express the same atomic claim.
The current contract does not encode each derivative text or its derivation edge.
The supplied trace does not establish whether additional independent observations exist for the target claim.

selection_rationale: The reversible selection preserves claim-level uncertainty and avoids treating publication count as independent evidence while the governing provenance frame remains ambiguous.
